design:
## Design tests

After the bench, the new drawings were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v026.md`, six pictures, three readers). The older man was "old man ... grey hair, blue-grey flat cap" or an "older man with grey hair in a blue-grey cap", with a remark on his face only on the seesaw pose. The dog at the door was "looking at the viewer as if waiting for a walk", with open eyes. Both newspaper dogs read as dogs reading, and the white one, "an odd white figure ... ghostly" in the v0.25 design tests, was now a "white dog with brown patches". The swept leaves read in all three pictures, though twice a reader asked where they came from: "the leaves do not obviously come from anywhere". No reader had a figure growing out of the lamp post or about to walk into it. No new rule came out of them, so there was no second round.
intro: The twenty-third screen read all 67 pictures, the set's 21 and 46 probes: 743 of 752 scored items had full marks, and one, in a probe, was misread. The gate went down: 59 of the 64 templates pass, against 61, with five failures against three. Two of v0.25's three failures now read in full, the dog at the door and the ducks' bread. The third got worse, and that is this release's own doing: `sweep` gained a heap of leaves and a fan of bristles, and one of its three readers saw "a long yellow-headed rake", at 0.67. It is first on the v0.27 list. The other four failures are on drawings this release did not change, each on one or two half marks and each in full in v0.25; the v0.9 retest put the gate's reader variance at about five templates between screens. The named complaints did fall. The older man's face drew one remark in his 12 pictures, against ten of his 21, no reader had the teenager's head on the wrong way round, and the newspaper dog was only ever a dog. Readers' remarks per picture fell for the first time since v0.23, from 5.93 to 5.27. That row is recounted here, because the counter had been taking bullets that say nothing is wrong for remarks: the rise published with v0.25 as 11% was 5%.
screen:
Across all 67 pictures 743 of 752 scored items had full marks. Eight had half marks, one was misread and none was missed. The misread is the broom: an older man raking leaves "with a long yellow-headed rake" (picture 37), where the two other readers of `sweep` said "sweeping up a pile of autumn leaves" and "sweeping a pile of red, orange and brown leaves with a long broom". Below full marks: a bearded man's ice cream, twice, "looking at or eating it" and "could be eating the ice cream or just holding it up"; a walker's obstacle, twice, as it "lies slightly off his line"; "binoculars or a camera"; a sprinkler's box as "a wooden crate standing in a puddle", with its soaking only one of two readings; and a person "sitting in mid-air or on the edge of the path". The set's headline falls a little with those: all items 0.988 (0.995), with inferences at 0.953 and the first contradiction below 1.00 since v0.21, each on a few half marks.

**The remarks row is recounted.** Sorting v0.25's remarks for this release's list showed that `summarize_screen.py` had counted bullets that say nothing is wrong (25 of v0.25's 428, 2 of v0.24's 408). The counter is fixed and the row recounted for every screen that has one, so its figures differ from those published before: v0.21 3.92 (4.35), v0.22 4.17 (4.49), v0.23 3.86 (4.32), v0.24 5.64 (5.67), v0.25 5.93 (6.29). v0.25's rise was 5%, not the 11% its README gave, and the v0.24 control's reader effect 18%, not 15%. On the corrected row remarks fell by 11% here. The remarks were not sorted by kind this time, so how much of the fall is the drawings and how much the readers is not separated. What they noticed most: a seesaw's plank through its sitter ("sitting right into the plank"), a hose "like a stiff loop standing in the air", water "like a beaded curtain", and faces hidden by a tilted head.
redrawn: `dog_wants_walk` and `dog_reading` read in full, and so did the feeders' bag: "a brown paper bag" or "a paper bag" for all six feeders in five pictures, with no cup or carton. `sandbox` read in full with no box or model. `ducks_bread` read in full, its v0.25 half marks probably scoring variance. `sweep` is the one this release made worse. The last four rows were not changed and each read in full in v0.25.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (56 in three, 3 in four, 2 in five, 3 in six), and 59 of 64 pass, down from 61. One failure, `sweep`, is a misread on what this release redrew. The other four are on unchanged drawings and each read in full in v0.25, and the v0.9 retest put the gate's reader variance at about five templates between screens, so those four do not by themselves show that anything got worse. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
inspection: Building and inspecting the set and the probes found nothing more to fix, but placement took more searching. The tier-4 garden and street placed again on their v0.25 seeds. The tier-4 park took 16 failed seeds, and the tier-4 playground 89 across two searches side by side, on the last seed of the second list (3 in v0.25). The tier-3 playground placed under template-variety steering, after seven failed seeds, where v0.24's and v0.25's needed the unsteered search. The tier-4 isomorph took 676 failed attempts (13 tries in v0.25). Why the playground got so much harder was not traced, and `vision/flaws_v026.md` says what was ruled out. The set's isomorphs are two at tier 2, two at tier 3 and one at tier 4. All 67 records rebuild identical to the pixel.
calib: The ducks' bread's cue salience moved by +0.025 and the newspaper dog's by +0.024, with their redraws; the bucket hat's by -0.010 and the trip's by -0.005, with no drawing of theirs changed; every other template's by less than 0.002.
